model_organism.citation: ASHG 2014 - Transcriptional consequences of 16p11.2 microdeletion/microduplication syndrome in mouse cortex converges on genes and pathways associated with autism and known intellectual disability syndromes (I. Blumenthal et al.)
model_organism.knockout_type: copy number variation model (CNV of syntenic 7qf3 region)
phenotypes: altered expression of TCF4 and other genes involved in synaptic function, chromatin modification, and transcriptional regulation
differential expression of genes involved in intellectual disability
perturbation of networks involved in autism spectrum disorder pathogenesis
enrichment for genes related to Joubert and Bardet-Biedl syndromes
model_organism.sample_size: 16 mice (4 del, 4 dup, 8 control) in initial study; expanded to 48 mice and 6 tissues
model_organism.significance: p = 2.36e-4 (Joubert syndrome enrichment); p = 0.046 (Bardet-Biedl syndrome enrichment); p = 0.025 (ciliary development pathways)

changes in TCF4 binding affinity due to altered cytosine modification
potential epigenetic impact on distal regulatory regions

model_organism.significance: 1113 common loss-of-5hmC regions; 2182 common gain-of-5hmC regions identified across disease models

biological.citation: Inhibition of neutrophil extracellular traps alleviates blood-brain barrier disruption and cognitive dysfunction via Wnt3/β-catenin/TCF4 signaling in sepsis-associated encephalopathy (PMID: 40102948)
biological.summary: TCF4 is a key component of the Wnt3/β-catenin/TCF4 signaling pathway that regulates blood-brain barrier integrity and cognitive function. NETs inhibition promotes VCL/β-catenin/VE-cadherin complex formation and increases Occludin expression through this pathway in a CLP-induced sepsis-associated encephalopathy mouse model.
biological.significance: Pathway identified as most significant in RNA-Seq analysis

biological.citation: Class I HDAC inhibitors enhance antitumor efficacy and persistence of CAR-T cells by activation of the Wnt pathway (PMID: 38578828)
biological.summary: TCF4 expression is upregulated by class I HDAC inhibitors (M344 and chidamide) in CAR-T cells, leading to activation of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway. Multi-omics analyses (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, H3K27ac CUT&Tag-seq) demonstrate that HDACi enhance H3K27ac activity at TCF4 locus and increase TCF4, LEF1, and CTNNB1 expression.
biological.sample_size: In vitro and in vivo CAR-T cell models

biological.citation: FOXP3 promotes tumor growth and metastasis by activating Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and EMT in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 28716029)
biological.summary: TCF4 physically interacts with β-catenin and FOXP3 to enhance Wnt signaling and promote transcription of target genes (c-Myc, Cyclin D1) in NSCLC cells. Co-immunoprecipitation demonstrates direct protein-protein interaction between FOXP3, β-catenin, and TCF4.
biological.significance: Co-IP confirmed physical interaction; high FOXP3 associated with decreased overall survival (p<0.05)

biological.citation: Liquidambaric acid inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling and colon cancer via targeting TNF receptor-associated factor 2 (PMID: 35108540)
biological.summary: TCF4 is a component of a TRAF2/β-catenin/TCF4/TNIK complex in colon cancer cells where it functions as a transcriptional effector of Wnt signaling. LDA treatment disrupts β-catenin/TCF4 interactions within this complex, inhibiting oncogenic Wnt signaling.
biological.sample_size: Colon cancer cell lines and in vivo models
biological.significance: Complex formation confirmed; LDA disrupts interactions

biological.citation: Transcription Factor 4 loss-of-function is associated with deficits in progenitor proliferation and cortical neuron content (PMID: 35501322)
biological.summary: TCF4 loss-of-function in patient-derived neural progenitor cells from Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome individuals reduces proliferation and neuronal differentiation capacity. TCF4 mutations decrease Wnt signaling and SOX gene expression, leading to reduced progenitor proliferation. Phenotypes are rescued by TCF4 correction or Wnt pathway modulation in brain organoids.
biological.sample_size: Patient-derived iPSC-derived neural progenitors and organoids from Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome children
biological.significance: Functional rescue demonstrated with TCF4 correction and Wnt pathway modulation

biological.citation: STING-mediated IL-6 Inhibits OATP1B1 Expression via the TCF4 Signaling Pathway in Cholestasis (PMID: 39130625)
biological.summary: TCF4 acts as a transcriptional regulator of OATP1B1 expression in hepatocytes. IL-6 downregulates β-catenin/TCF4 complex, leading to decreased OATP1B1 expression. siRNA knockdown of β-catenin/TCF4 confirms their role in OATP1B1 regulation in cholestatic disease.
biological.sample_size: Cholestatic mouse model; PLC/PRF/5 and HepG2 hepatocyte cell lines
biological.significance: siRNA knockdown confirms β-catenin/TCF4 involvement in OATP1B1 regulation

biological.summary: TCF4 is a regulatory component of the transcriptional complex composed of β-catenin and TCF4 that mediates Wnt/β-catenin signaling in colorectal cancer. TNIK is a regulatory kinase that interacts with this β-catenin/TCF4 complex to enable transcription of Wnt target genes.
biological.significance: TNIK identified as essential regulatory component of β-catenin/TCF4 complex

biological.citation: Suppression of TCF4 promotes a ZC3H12A-mediated self-sustaining inflammatory feedback cycle involving IL-17RA/IL-17RE epidermal signaling (PMID: 38470486)
biological.summary: TCF4 acts as a negative regulator of IL-17C transcription in human keratinocytes. siRNA knockdown of TCF4 increases IL17C expression, and IL-17C stimulation decreases TCF4 protein levels, creating a feedback loop. TCF4 suppression also increases ZC3H12A and NFKBIZ expression, promoting proinflammatory responses.
biological.sample_size: Human keratinocytes; KC-Tie2 inflammatory dermatitis mouse model
biological.significance: siRNA knockdown confirms TCF4 as negative regulator of IL-17C; genetic elimination of IL-17 pathway components reverses TCF4 changes

biological.summary: TCF4 overexpression in umbilical cord blood cells increases erythroid colony-forming units (CFU-Es) twofold, while TCF4 knockdown dramatically decreases erythroid colonies. TCF4 does not affect granulocyte, macrophage, or granulocyte-macrophage colonies. MDS patients with high TCF4 expression have higher hemoglobin levels than those with low expression.
biological.sample_size: Umbilical cord blood cells; MDS patient samples (n=patients with high vs. low TCF4)
biological.significance: TCF4 overexpression increases CFU-Es twofold; MDS patients with high TCF4 have higher Hb (9.0 vs. 8.55 g/dL, p=0.02)

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Deciphering the genetic architecture of autism spectrum disorder using chromosomal microarray and whole exome sequencing in patient-parent trios in India
biological.summary: TCF4 is identified as a gene harboring de novo loss-of-function mutations in autism spectrum disorder patients. TCF4 de novo SNVs were found in the cohort of 101 ASD patient-parent trios, with 35.2% of de novo SNVs predicted to be loss-of-function variants.
biological.significance: TCF4 identified among previously known ASD genes with de novo mutations; 90% of diagnosed cases had SNVs

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Phenotypic effects of common coding copy-number variation (PMID: UK Biobank study)
biological.summary: An intronic trinucleotide repeat expansion within TCF4 associates with altered levels of multiple serum biomarkers (creatinine, urate, HbA1c, testosterone), blood counts, BMI, and FEV1/FVC ratio. This repeat expansion, previously implicated in Fuchs corneal dystrophy, also associates with increased cataract risk.
biological.significance: TCF4 repeat expansion associated with multiple phenotypes (p=2.4×10⁻¹⁶ to 6.9×10⁻¹⁰); cataract risk p=3.5×10⁻⁹
